If sentiment is negative in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overestimating rebound.  
If sentiment is positive and price is rising, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to capture momentum.  
If sentiment is neutral and price is flat, apply no adjustment for early horizon but reduce by 0.5–1.0% for late horizon (16–30 days) to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is negative and price is falling, reduce forecast by 1.0–2.0% for late horizon to avoid underestimating crash risk.  
If sentiment is positive and price is falling, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for mid horizon to counteract sentiment-driven overcorrection.  
If sentiment is neutral and price is rising, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon to capture sentiment lag.
